background_notes.fact: For the real mean-zero datum u0 in S001 with gamma>0 and ||u0||_(H^gamma)<=R, u0m=P_leq(m)u0 is a smooth real mean-zero trigonometric polynomial, ||u0m||_(H^gamma)<=R, and u0m tends to u0 in H^gamma and L2. Also ||u0m||_2+||u0||_2<=2R.

grounds.reason: L1 supplies membership, reality, zero mean and the radius bound; u0m is defined as the symmetric Fourier truncation.
The weighted squared Fourier norm is summable; reality is conjugate symmetry and zero mean is vanishing zero coefficient.
L2 is H^0 with the same normalization.

background_notes.justification: The retained set of integer frequencies is finite and invariant under k->-k, so its Fourier sum is smooth and preserves conjugate symmetry and the zero coefficient. Its norm squared is a sub-sum of the original nonnegative series. The squared H^gamma norm of the difference is the tail of that convergent series and tends to zero. Since <k>^(2gamma)>=1, the L2 norm of any such difference is at most its H^gamma norm, and both initial L2 norms are at most R.

background_notes.fact: For the fixed tau=T/Lsteps>0 in S002, the iterates u_m^n=Psi_tau^n(u0m) converge in L2 to u^n=Psi_tau^n(u0) for every 0<=n<=Lsteps. Together with the exact-flow convergence and the common smooth-data bound K=C*tau^gamma, this implies max_(0<=n<=Lsteps)||uexact(n*tau)-u^n||_2<=K.

grounds.reason: T>0, together with the positive integer fixed in S001, makes tau positive.
F001 provides initial L2 convergence and uniform-in-time exact-flow convergence, with all approximants in the same ball.
For every fixed positive tau, Psi_tau is a continuous self-map on mean-zero L2, preserving reality; all finite iterates exist.
N013 bounds the smooth-data grid errors by the same C*tau^gamma.
The numerical states are precisely successive applications of Psi_tau.
Lsteps and tau are fixed throughout the approximation limit, and tau<=tau0.

background_notes.justification: The induction base is u0m->u0. Applying continuity of the self-map Psi_tau to convergence at level n gives convergence at level n+1 and keeps every iterate in its domain. At a fixed grid point, the absolute difference between the approximate and limiting error norms is at most ||uapprox_m(n*tau)-uexact(n*tau)||_2+||u_m^n-u^n||_2 by the triangle inequality, hence tends to zero. A limit of real numbers bounded above by the fixed K is at most K. This holds for each of the finitely many grid indices, so their maximum is at most K; no limiting operation in tau is involved.
